# Amalfi Coast Travel — Complete Reference Guide

> Source: amalficoast-travel.com | Independent travel guide for the Amalfi Coast, Sorrento Peninsula, and Gulf Islands. Published in 5 languages (EN, IT, DE, ES, FR). All distances, times, and prices verified for 2025-2026 travel season.

---

## GEOGRAPHY & OVERVIEW

The Amalfi Coast (Costiera Amalfitana) is a 50 km stretch of coastline along the southern edge of the Sorrentine Peninsula in the province of Salerno, Campania, Italy. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997. It runs from Positano in the west to Vietri sul Mare in the east along the SS163 state road (also called "Nastro Azzurro").

The Sorrentine Peninsula separates the Gulf of Naples (north) from the Gulf of Salerno (south). Length: approximately 77 km. Highest point: Monte Faito (497 m). Main towns: Sorrento, Vico Equense, Massa Lubrense, Sant'Agnello.

The Gulf Islands comprise Capri (area: 10.4 km²), Ischia (area: 46.3 km², largest island in the Bay of Naples), and Procida (area: 4 km², smallest inhabited island in the bay).

---

## DESTINATIONS — AMALFI COAST

### Amalfi
- Population: ~5,000 | Elevation: 6 m
- Key sights: Cathedral of Sant'Andrea (9th century, Arab-Norman style), Paper Museum (Museo della Carta), Piazza Duomo
- History: Once a powerful Maritime Republic (839-1131 AD) rivaling Venice, Genoa, and Pisa. Invented the maritime compass (Flavio Gioia, though disputed). The Tabula Amalphitana was the oldest maritime code in the Mediterranean.
- Transport: SITA bus from Salerno (~75 min) or Sorrento (~100 min). Ferry from Salerno (~35 min), Positano (~25 min), Capri (~80 min seasonal).

### Positano
- Population: ~3,800 | Elevation: 100 m (town center)
- Key sights: Spiaggia Grande, Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta (majolica dome), Fornillo Beach, Path of the Gods trailhead (Nocelle)
- History: Prosperous trading port in the 16th-17th centuries, declined into a fishing village, rediscovered by artists and writers (John Steinbeck's 1953 Harper's Bazaar essay). Moda Positano fashion industry born in the 1960s.
- Transport: SITA bus from Sorrento (~50 min) or Amalfi (~40 min). Ferry from Capri (~30 min), Amalfi (~25 min), Naples Beverello (~80 min seasonal).

### Ravello
- Population: ~2,400 | Elevation: 350 m
- Key sights: Villa Rufolo (13th century, inspiration for Wagner's Parsifal garden), Villa Cimbrone (Terrace of Infinity), Ravello Festival (classical music, July-September since 1953)
- Note: Ravello has no direct sea access. Reached by bus from Amalfi (25 min, hairpin road). No ferry service.

### Praiano
- Population: ~2,000 | Elevation: 120 m
- Key sights: Marina di Praia (small cove beach), Sentiero degli Dei (Path of the Gods) western trailhead, Chiesa di San Gennaro
- Character: Quieter, more affordable alternative to Positano. Popular with returning visitors who prefer authenticity over glamour.

### Maiori
- Population: ~5,500
- Key sights: Longest beach on the Amalfi Coast (approximately 300 m of sand). Torre Normanna. Less touristy than Positano/Amalfi.

### Minori
- Population: ~2,700
- Key sights: Roman Villa (Villa Marittima, 1st century AD, well-preserved mosaic floors), traditional pastry shops (sfogliatella Santa Rosa origin area)

### Vietri sul Mare
- Population: ~8,000
- Key sights: Gateway to the Amalfi Coast from Salerno. Famous for hand-painted ceramics (maiolica tradition since the 15th century). Ceramic Museum.

### Cetara
- Population: ~2,200
- Key sights: Fishing village famous for colatura di alici DOP (anchovy sauce, heir to Roman garum). Active fishing fleet. Annual Anchovy Festival.

---

## DESTINATIONS — SORRENTO PENINSULA

### Sorrento
- Population: ~16,500 | Elevation: 50 m
- Key sights: Piazza Tasso, Chiostro di San Francesco (14th century), Marina Grande fishing port, limoncello production
- Transport hub: Circumvesuviana train from Naples Centrale (~70 min, ~EUR 3.90). Hydrofoil to Capri (~25 min), Naples Beverello (~35 min), Positano (~35 min seasonal). SITA bus to Amalfi Coast.
- Strategic position: Capri 25 min by hydrofoil, Pompeii 30 min by Circumvesuviana, Naples 70 min, Amalfi <2 hours.

### Vico Equense
- Population: ~20,000
- Key sights: Birthplace of pizza al metro (pizza by the meter) at Da Gigino since 1953. Castello Giusso (medieval castle on cliff). Aequa Roman ruins.

### Massa Lubrense
- Population: ~14,000
- Southernmost municipality on the peninsula. Punta Campanella (tip of the peninsula, Temple of Athena site). Marina del Cantone beach. Gateway to Ieranto bay (FAI protected).

### Sant'Agnello
- Population: ~9,000
- Between Sorrento and Piano di Sorrento. Historic villas, quieter alternative to Sorrento center.

---

## DESTINATIONS — GULF ISLANDS

### Capri
- Area: 10.4 km² | Highest point: Monte Solaro (589 m)
- Population: ~14,000 (Capri + Anacapri)
- Key sights: Blue Grotto (Grotta Azzurra), Faraglioni (three iconic rock formations, tallest 109 m), Via Krupp (1902, built by Friedrich Alfred Krupp), Augustus Gardens, Villa Jovis (Tiberius' imperial palace, 1st century AD), Monte Solaro chairlift from Anacapri
- Anacapri: Upper town at 275 m elevation. Villa San Michele (Axel Munthe). Church of San Michele (majolica floor, 1761). Monte Solaro chairlift.
- The Faraglioni: Three limestone stacks — Faraglione di Terra (109 m, connected to coast), Faraglione di Mezzo (82 m, with natural arch ~40 m long), Faraglione di Fuori/Scopolo (104 m, home to the endemic blue lizard Podarcis sicula coerulea)
- Transport: Hydrofoil from Sorrento (~25 min), Naples Beverello (~50 min), Positano (~30 min seasonal). No cars for non-residents.

### Ischia
- Area: 46.3 km² | Highest point: Monte Epomeo (788 m, dormant volcano)
- Population: ~60,000 across 6 comuni
- Key sights: Aragonese Castle (built 474 BC, rebuilt 1441), thermal spas (over 100 hot springs), Spiaggia dei Maronti (3 km, longest beach, volcanic black sand with fumaroles up to 60°C), Forio (westernmost town, La Mortella gardens, Soccorso church)
- History: Ancient Greek colony of Pithecusae (8th century BC), first Greek colony in the western Mediterranean. 1883 earthquake (magnitude 5.8) at Casamicciola led to Italy's first seismic building codes.
- Thermal waters: Volcanic origin. Over 100 thermal springs. Notable: Cavascura canyon (natural thermal spa behind Maronti beach), Negombo thermal park, Poseidon Gardens.

### Procida
- Area: 4 km² | Population: ~10,000
- Key sights: Marina Corricella (pastel-colored fishermen's port, filming location), Terra Murata (medieval citadel, highest point), Cala del Pozzo Vecchio (Il Postino beach, 1994 film with Massimo Troisi)
- Italian Capital of Culture 2022. Smallest inhabited island in the Bay of Naples. Strong fishing tradition. Graziella festival (literary character by Lamartine, 1852).

---

## BEACHES — KEY FACTS

### Amalfi Coast Beaches
- **Fiordo di Furore**: Dramatic gorge beach. 30 m wide. Access: steep stairs (500+ steps) or boat. Annual international diving competition.
- **Spiaggia Grande Positano**: Main beach, ~300 m. Pebble/sand mix. Ferry landing point. Beach clubs and free sections.
- **Santa Croce Amalfi**: Hidden cove near Amalfi. Boat or free shuttle access. Crystal-clear water.
- **Marina di Praia**: Small cove between cliffs in Praiano. Popular diving spot. One restaurant.

### Sorrento Peninsula Beaches
- **Bagni della Regina Giovanna**: Natural pool inside Roman ruins (Villa of Pollio Felice, 1st century AD, described by poet Statius). Rocky access, 20-minute trail through olive groves. Free, no services. Named after Queen Giovanna I of Anjou (1326-1382).
- **Marina del Cantone**: Largest beach on the peninsula. Pebble beach. Famous for Spaghetti alla Nerano (pasta with fried zucchini, created at Ristorante Maria Grazia in 1952). Departure point for Ieranto bay.
- **Cala di Mitigliano**: 300 steps down through Mediterranean scrub. White pebbles. Best view of Capri from a beach.
- **Baia di Ieranto**: FAI-protected bay. Hiking access only (40 min from Nerano). Marine protected area. Stunning Capri views.

### Island Beaches
- **Marina Piccola Capri**: Capri's main swimming area. La Canzone del Mare beach club (founded 1932 by Gracie Fields). Best close-up view of the Faraglioni. Shaded after 4 PM. Scoglio delle Sirene (legendary Sirens' rock from Homer's Odyssey). Emperor Augustus first landed on Capri here.
- **Spiaggia dei Maronti (Ischia)**: 3 km, longest on the island. Volcanic black sand heated by underground fumaroles (up to 60°C). Cavascura thermal canyon accessible from eastern end. Water taxi from Sant'Angelo (5 min).
- **Cala del Pozzo Vecchio (Procida)**: Filming location of Il Postino (1994, dir. Michael Radford, starring Massimo Troisi and Philippe Noiret). Black volcanic sand. Troisi died 12 hours after completing filming. 5 Oscar nominations, 1 win (Best Score, Luis Bacalov).
- **Faraglioni di Capri**: Three iconic rock formations (not a beach). Boat tours pass through the natural arch of Faraglione di Mezzo. Tradition: couples kiss under the arch for good luck. Home to the endemic blue lizard.

---

## TRANSPORT

### Circumvesuviana Train
- Route: Naples Centrale (Garibaldi) to Sorrento
- Duration: ~70 minutes | Price: ~EUR 3.90 (2025)
- Stops: Ercolano Scavi (Herculaneum), Pompei Scavi (Pompeii), Torre Annunziata, Castellammare di Stabia, Vico Equense, Meta, Sorrento
- Frequency: Every 30-40 minutes
- Operator: EAV (Ente Autonomo Volturno)

### Ferries & Hydrofoils
- Sorrento-Capri: ~25 min hydrofoil (Caremar, SNAV, Alilauro, NLG)
- Naples Beverello-Capri: ~50 min hydrofoil, ~80 min ferry
- Naples Beverello-Ischia: ~50 min hydrofoil, ~90 min ferry
- Naples Beverello-Procida: ~35 min hydrofoil, ~60 min ferry
- Sorrento-Naples: ~35 min hydrofoil
- Sorrento-Positano: ~35 min (seasonal, April-October)
- Salerno-Amalfi: ~35 min ferry
- Positano-Amalfi: ~25 min ferry
- Operators: Caremar, SNAV, Alilauro, NLG, Travelmar, Lucibello

### SITA Bus (Amalfi Coast)
- Route: Sorrento to Amalfi via SS163 (Amalfi Drive)
- Duration: ~100 minutes end to end
- Key stops: Meta, Positano, Praiano, Furore, Amalfi
- Tickets: Purchase before boarding at tabacchi shops. EUR 2.00-2.80 depending on distance.
- Tips: Very crowded in summer. Sit on the right side (sea side) going from Sorrento to Amalfi.

### Driving
- SS163 (Amalfi Drive): Narrow, winding, spectacular. 50 km from Vietri to Positano. Many sections single-lane with passing places.
- ZTL (Zona Traffico Limitato): Active in Positano, Amalfi, Ravello, Sorrento center during summer months. Fines for unauthorized entry.
- Recommendation: Avoid driving July-August. Use ferries and buses instead. Parking is scarce and expensive (EUR 5-8/hour in peak season).
- Naples to Sorrento by car: ~1 hour without traffic via A3 motorway.

---

## HIKING

### Path of the Gods (Sentiero degli Dei)
- Route: Agerola (Bomerano) to Nocelle (above Positano)
- Distance: 7.5 km | Duration: 3-4 hours | Elevation: 580 m start, 450 m finish
- Difficulty: Moderate. Some exposed sections (vertigo warning). No shade for most of the trail.
- Season: March to November (avoid July-August midday heat). Best: April-May, September-October.
- Access: SITA bus to Agerola from Amalfi. Return from Nocelle by local bus to Positano or 1,700 steps down.

### Punta Campanella
- Tip of the Sorrentine Peninsula. Site of ancient Temple of Athena (Greek) / Minerva (Roman).
- Trail from Massa Lubrense (Termini): ~45 min one way.
- Marine Protected Area. Capri visible across the strait (~5 km).

---

## FOOD & DRINK

### Signature Dishes
- **Spaghetti alla Nerano**: Pasta with fried zucchini and Provolone del Monaco cheese. Created by Maria Grazia at Marina del Cantone in 1952.
- **Delizia al Limone**: Lemon-shaped sponge cake filled with lemon cream. Signature dessert of the coast.
- **Colatura di Alici di Cetara DOP**: Fermented anchovy sauce, heir to ancient Roman garum. Produced in Cetara.
- **Pizza al Metro**: Pizza sold by the meter, invented in Vico Equense at Da Gigino (since 1953).
- **Limoncello**: Lemon liqueur made from Sfusato Amalfitano lemons (IGP). Traditionally served ice-cold after meals.
- **Sfusato Amalfitano**: IGP lemon variety unique to the Amalfi Coast. Larger and more aromatic than common lemons. Grown on terraced gardens (limoneti) protected by straw mats (pagliarelle).

### Wine
- **Costa d'Amalfi DOC**: Three sub-zones: Furore, Ravello, Tramonti. Heroic viticulture on terraced hillsides.
- Key grapes: Falanghina, Biancolella (white); Piedirosso, Aglianico (red).
- Notable producer: Marisa Cuomo (Furore), Gran Furor Divina Costiera.

---

## PRACTICAL INFO

### Best Time to Visit
- **Peak season**: July-August. Hottest, most crowded, highest prices. Avg temp: 28-32°C.
- **Shoulder season**: April-June, September-October. Best balance of weather, crowds, prices. Sea warm enough for swimming May-October.
- **Off-season**: November-March. Many hotels/restaurants closed. Cooler (10-15°C). Ferries reduced. Good for hiking and cultural visits.
- **Sea temperature**: 18°C (May), 24°C (July), 26°C (August-September), 22°C (October).

### Budget (2025-2026 estimates)
- Budget hotel/B&B: EUR 80-150/night
- Mid-range hotel: EUR 150-300/night
- Luxury hotel: EUR 400-1,500+/night
- Restaurant meal: EUR 15-25 (casual), EUR 40-80 (upscale)
- SITA bus ticket: EUR 2.00-2.80
- Circumvesuviana: EUR 3.90 (Naples-Sorrento)
- Hydrofoil Sorrento-Capri: EUR 20-25
- Beach club sunbed: EUR 15-50/day depending on location
